findings.title: Shared levels are downloaded and uploaded over plain HTTP
findings.entry_point: The download starts automatically when MyTreasurePanel.init() creates MyTreasureUserLevels and calls loadUserlevels() at Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Android/myTreasureAndroid/src/com/apogames/mytreasure/game/MyTreasurePanel.java:140-143. Upload data originates from the editor at game/MyTreasureEditor.java:238-251.
findings.sink: URLConnection.openConnection() is reached for upload at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:149-150 and download at :190-191. The resolved endpoints are explicitly http:// at MyTreasureConstants.java:12-13.
findings.data_path: Startup follows MyTreasurePanel.init() at game/MyTreasurePanel.java:140-143 -> MyTreasurePanel.loadUserlevels() at :390-397 -> MyTreasureUserLevels.loadUserlevels() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserLevels.java:47-50 -> MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:181-207. Upload follows MyTreasureEditor.uploadString() at game/MyTreasureEditor.java:250-254 -> MyTreasureUserLevels.addLevel() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserLevels.java:120-123 -> MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.save() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:141-165.
findings.attack_scenario: On a hostile Wi-Fi network, an attacker intercepts the initial HTTP POST to get_level.php and replaces its response with attacker-selected level records. The attacker can also alter or suppress the URL-encoded level body written at MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:160-163 during upload. They gain control over downloaded shared content and the integrity of level submissions; parser-specific crash and exhaustion consequences are separated below.
findings.preconditions: The device must report an active connection as checked at MyTreasureActivity.java:42-46, the endpoint must be reachable, and the Android build/runtime must permit cleartext HTTP. The attacker must control or intercept the network path; a malicious endpoint operator also satisfies the trust condition.
findings.validation_plan: Run the non-free activity on an emulator configured through an HTTP interception proxy. Route www.apo-games.de:80 through the proxy, launch the app, and confirm an unencrypted POST containing Get= to /myTreasure/get_level.php. Replace the response with one complete 11-line record and verify it appears under Userlevels. Then create and upload an editor level and confirm the proxy can read and modify the level= form body before it reaches save_level.php.

findings.title: Malformed downloaded level crashes the unchecked level-string parser
findings.code_excerpt: this.level[y][x] = Integer.valueOf(levelString.substring(y * this.level[0].length + x + 4, y * this.level[0].length + x + 5));
findings.entry_point: The untrusted level string is the first line of each 11-line server record read at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:210-212. The source may be a malicious shared-level server or an HTTP response modified in transit.
findings.sink: MyTreasureGame.loadLevel() performs unchecked substring and numeric conversions at game/MyTreasureGame.java:175-186, including the Integer.valueOf() call at line 186. No exception handler surrounds this interactive load path.
findings.data_path: MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the response at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:210-232 -> MyTreasureUserLevels.loadUserlevels() copies it into MyTreasureLevels.editorLevels at userlevels/MyTreasureUserLevels.java:47-57 and :68-78 -> the Userlevels menu is entered at game/MyTreasureMenu.java:90-94 -> a selected item calls setGame() at game/MyTreasureLevelChooser.java:237-239 -> MyTreasurePanel.setGame() invokes loadLevel() at game/MyTreasurePanel.java:271-283 -> the downloaded string is selected at game/MyTreasureGame.java:139-147 and parsed at :175-186.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker returns a syntactically complete 11-line record whose level line is 0101x0000 and whose other ten fields are valid numbers/text. Loading and sorting succeed, so the level becomes selectable. When the victim selects it, width, height, gold, and silver parse successfully, but the tile x reaches Integer.valueOf() at MyTreasureGame.java:186, producing an uncaught NumberFormatException and terminating or disabling the game execution thread.
findings.preconditions: A complete record must pass the outer 11-field loader, the non-free activity must be in use because MyTreasureMenu.java:90-94 gates Userlevels on FREE_VERSION, and the victim must select the malicious level. A network attacker additionally requires cleartext HTTP to be permitted.
findings.validation_plan: Intercept get_level.php and return these newline-delimited fields: 0101x0000, 1.0, 0, 0, attacker, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0.0. Wait for the Userlevels button, open it, and select the first level. An uncaught NumberFormatException whose top application frame is MyTreasureGame.java:186, accompanied by game exit or a dead game thread, confirms the issue.

findings.title: Unbounded shared-level response can exhaust application memory
findings.entry_point: An attacker-controlled get_level.php response is read automatically following MyTreasurePanel.java:140-143 and :390-397; no user selection is needed.
findings.sink: The EOF-controlled loop at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:210-235 continually appends response data to eleven ArrayLists at :212-232 without a byte, line, or record limit. OutOfMemoryError is not covered by the IOException-only handler at :238-242.
findings.data_path: MyTreasurePanel.init() at game/MyTreasurePanel.java:140-143 -> MyTreasurePanel.loadUserlevels() at :390-397 -> MyTreasureUserLevels.loadUserlevels() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserLevels.java:47-50 -> MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load() at userlevels/MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.java:181-235 -> repeated readLine(), numeric conversion, and ArrayList.add() operations.
findings.attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP interceptor sends an indefinitely chunked response consisting of repeated valid 11-line records and never closes it. The background loader retains every parsed String, Integer, and Float in its lists. Heap use rises until Android kills the process or Java throws an uncaught OutOfMemoryError, denying use of the game merely by launching it online.
findings.preconditions: The app must launch while online, the attacker must control the response stream or network path, and cleartext HTTP must be allowed when exploiting via interception. Records must contain valid numeric fields so parsing continues.
findings.validation_plan: Proxy get_level.php to an HTTP handler that repeatedly emits a valid 11-line record such as 010110000 plus ten valid metadata lines, flushes each batch, and keeps the body open. Launch the app and monitor its process with Android Studio Memory Profiler or adb shell dumpsys meminfo. Continuously increasing heap followed by OutOfMemoryError or process death, with MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load() active, confirms the issue.

findings.title: Locally editable skull count is trusted to unlock difficulty tiers
findings.entry_point: A local user modifies the MytreasurePref SharedPreferences file named at MyTreasureConstants.java:17. It is opened with mode 0 at MyTreasureActivity.java:26, so this is not network-reachable and requires access to the app-private data sandbox.
findings.sink: MyTreasureMap.touchedReleased() treats getCurSkulls() as authoritative in its medium, hard, and very-hard unlock decisions at game/MyTreasureMap.java:156-168, :169-180, and :181-192.
findings.data_path: MyTreasureActivity obtains MytreasurePref at MyTreasureActivity.java:26 -> MyTreasurePanel.loadProperties() reads skulls without validation at game/MyTreasurePanel.java:164-175 -> getCurSkulls() returns the value at :217-219 -> MyTreasureMap compares it with the 40/140/280 thresholds declared at game/MyTreasureMap.java:48-52 and opens the corresponding level chooser at :156-192.
findings.attack_scenario: On a rooted, debuggable, or otherwise sandbox-accessible installation, the local player stops the app and changes the stored skulls value to 280. After relaunch, all three threshold checks succeed, allowing the player to enter later difficulty tiers without solving the prerequisite levels. This is local cheating only; it does not affect another user or the remote service.
findings.preconditions: The attacker must be the local device user and must have a way to edit app-private SharedPreferences, such as root, a genuinely debuggable package, or a permitted backup/restore path. The non-free activity must be used because each later-tier branch also checks !FREE_VERSION at MyTreasureMap.java:157, :170, and :182.
findings.validation_plan: Use a rooted emulator or confirmed debuggable build, force-stop the app, and edit its MytreasurePref XML so skulls is 280; optionally set levelchooser_step to 12. Relaunch, choose Play, and tap the medium, hard, and very-hard map regions. Access to each corresponding level chooser without completing prerequisite levels confirms the trust bypass.

notes: The supplied root contains 109 Java files: 29 variant/generated files and 80 files from duplicate extracted dependency trees. No AndroidManifest.xml or project configuration is present, so the target SDK's cleartext policy, manifest debuggability, backup policy, permissions, and exported components cannot be resolved. The generated BuildConfig says DEBUG=true at Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Android/myTreasureAndroid/gen/com/apogames/mytreasure/BuildConfig.java:5, but that alone does not prove the packaged APK is debuggable. Extracted modplug code exposes a native byte parser at _from_jar_andmodplug-1.0/com/peculiargames/andmodplug/PlayerThread.java:878 and loads a constant library at :912, but no target game source imports or calls it; the reachable music implementation instead uses a packaged raw resource and MediaPlayer.create() at Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Android/myTreasureAndroid/src/com/apogames/mytreasure/MyTreasureMusicPlayer.java:15 and :54. Therefore no untrusted entry point into the native parser was found and it was not reported as an unsafe_native_call.
